FlyRank AI · Self-paced program capstone

Search Performance Analysis

A review queue for pages losing search visibility, with a client-wide check to help editors decide where to start.

Python, DuckDB SQL, pandas, scikit-learn

Read the research paper View the GitHub repository ↗

The problem

A page losing impressions may be part of a wider decline across a client’s pages. I wanted to help editors decide whether to inspect one page, investigate a shared pattern, or gather more data first.

How I tested it

I used DuckDB to audit and aggregate about 23 million daily records from May and June 2026. The rule ranked pages using May impressions, click-through rate, and average position. I compared it with logistic regression on held-out clients, using a drop of more than 20% in June impressions as the outcome. A separate end-of-June check looked for widespread declines across each eligible client’s pages.

Results

I produced a review queue of 96,678 pages and flagged 14 of 32 eligible clients for broader investigation. On one client-disjoint test split, the rule reached 95% precision@20 for observed June declines, compared with 80% for logistic regression. The held-out decline rate was 65.5%.

What the results tell us

Keeping clients together in the split gave me a check on unseen clients at the same cutoff. The analysis covered one time window. The flags are prompts to investigate possible causes, and the study did not measure whether refreshing a page would recover impressions.
